edit.description: `segment` (189) cuts on every `/` rather than `splitn(4, '/')`, and the **count** decides the grain: odd is a member address, even a leaf's, because every name, key and leaf is one segment. `parse_nested_address` (219) accepts any odd count — the host is every segment but the final two, carried verbatim and itself a member address, so its `(host_kind, host_name)` is read at the host's own grain (a nested host's identity *is* its whole address, which is exactly what `address_of` round-trips) rather than off a first-colon split that would take `area` / `a/page/b`. `parse_leaf_address` takes the final segment as the whole leaf: `ParsedLeaf::child_path` keeps its dots and carries no `/` (`extract.rs`'s `addressed_leaves` joins with `.`), so the doc comment's slash claim and the module header's fixed-three spelling move with the re-cut.

`resolve` (217), the `Species` classifier, gates member-identity equality behind `nested_key(target).is_some()` (251) — three segments exactly — and then falls through to `parse_leaf_address`, so a five-segment member address answers "No leaf … is in the surface's serialized nested-member leaves" with no corpus consulted (the refactor capture's probe, verified at HEAD on a one-layer corpus). The member grain is tried at any odd count ahead of the leaf branch; the four-segment comment at 249 states the parity rule instead, and the `target.contains('/')` malformed fallthrough stays as the malformation's own voice.

`node_from_address` (1770) tries leaf then nested on the ordering the parity rule replaces, and `edge_host` (656) / `embedded_hosts_by_key` (2213) read a nested host through `embedded_source_host`, whose pair must name a nested host's own kind and its whole address. The three-segment narration at 1762 and 2100 moves with the reader; `address_of` at 2363 is unchanged.
`explain` over a five-segment target answers at member grain — the probe the refactor capture ran at HEAD, inverted.
The node-species assertion's home if `node_from_address`'s re-cut needs one beyond the grammar's own unit tests: a five-segment address is a member node, a four-segment one a leaf node.

`nested_member_key_segment` (118) is this parity rule's own refusal, and its doc comment (100) justifies it by *precedence* — "leaf grain is what the readers try first (`crate::graph`'s `node_from_address`, `crate::read`'s species split)" — the exact ordering this entry retires. Under parity a `/`-bearing key spells an even-count address, which is leaf grain by construction and no member address at all, so the rationale is restated as parity; the judge's behaviour and its diagnostic text are unchanged, and `address_of` at 220 is a verify-only read.

`a_key_that_is_not_one_address_segment_is_a_malformed_lock` (1062) is that judge's lane and its comment (1068) carries the same leaf-first narration, which moves with the judge's. The `parse_leaf_address` reads at 1262 and 1273 are four-segment and stand; `embedded_hosts_by_key` at 1127 is a call site the reader re-cut leaves alone.

summary: Segment count decides an address's grain — odd is a member, even a leaf — so the engine's one reader reads any depth instead of capping at three segments

tests.asserts: a member address reads at five and seven segments, a leaf address at four and six, and an empty segment still names nothing at either grain
`explain` on a five-segment target narrates the member-grain refusal, not the leaf reader's

acceptance: `cargo test` green, with the grammar's own tests reading both grains at any depth and `explain` answering a five-segment target at member grain rather than as a leaf.
